messages:
Lauren (CS): Hey team, Acme is seeing weird values from our /v1/rerank endpoint — negative scores and some >1, plus they expected probabilities. They've opened an escalation.
Acme Support (customer): @lauren here's the sample we got back. We send 5 candidates, get scores like -2.4, 0.7, 0.1. We assumed scores are probabilities 0..1. Can you explain? This is high-priority (billing impact). :frowning:
Lauren (CS): Copying the thread. Can someone from eng/ML confirm what the rerank score semantics are and how customers should interpret them?
Devon (ENG): Thanks — can you paste the exact request/response (sanitized) so we can repro quickly? Also what model are you hitting and any query prep steps?
Acme Support (customer): Sure — simplified curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-re-rank-1","query":"how to reset password","candidates":["click profile","contact support","reset via link","reset in settings","forgot password"]}'
```
Response (trimmed):
```json
{"candidates":[{"text":"reset via link","score":-2.4},{"text":"click profile","score":0.7},{"text":"forgot password","score":0.1}, ...]}
```
Lauren (CS): They also said sometimes scores are 0.0001 or 3.2 — very inconsistent.
Devon (ENG): Ok good repro. Jia (ML) can you take a look? My quick read: those are raw model scores/logits or log-prob differences, not normalized probabilities. Negative is fine — it's relative score. But let's confirm the exact transform our rerank pipeline returns.
Jia (ML): Confirming: the internal reranker returns the model's logit (actually log-odds vs a baseline) for each candidate. We currently surface that raw number in the `score` field. It's not normalized across the batch and not bounded to [0,1]. Negative values mean the model prefers the baseline over that candidate (or lower relative score). Positive means more preferred.
Paul (SRE): Adding that different models and tokenization contexts can change scale — one model's logits may be ~[-10, +5], another ~[-3, +3], so absolute numbers aren't comparable between models.
Lauren (CS): So we should communicate that to the customer and provide a short recipe to turn these into probabilities. Jia, can you draft sample code they can run client-side?
Jia (ML): Yep. Short guidance we should give: treat the scores as unnormalized logit-like scores. If you want probabilities across candidates, compute softmax across the returned scores: p_i = exp(score_i) / sum_j exp(score_j). Example (from their numbers): scores = [-2.4, 0.7, 0.1] -> exp = [0.090, 2.01, 1.105] -> probs = [0.032, 0.708, 0.389] (normalized across all candidates). Note sums to 1.
Jia (ML): Also warn about numerical stability for large positive/negative values — subtract max(score) before exponentiating: p_i = exp(score_i - max_score) / sum_j exp(score_j - max_score).
Devon (ENG): Good. Also mention that if they want a 0..1 confidence per candidate independent of other candidates, we don't provide calibrated probabilities out of the box. We can suggest a couple options: 1) run pairwise comparisons to get calibrated ranking; 2) fine-tune/calibrate a small logistic regressor on a labeled set mapping raw scores to probabilities; 3) ask us about an upcoming flag to return `normalized_scores=true` (internal note: product to consider).
Acme Support (customer): That helps — can you provide the code snippet we can paste into our app?
Jia (ML): Sample JS (very small):
```js
const scores = [-2.4, 0.7, 0.1];
const max = Math.max(...scores);
const exps = scores.map(s => Math.exp(s - max));
const sum = exps.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0);
const probs = exps.map(e => e / sum);
console.log(probs); // [0.032, 0.708, 0.389]
```
Devon (ENG): Also include a note: if your app expects values in [0,1] as independent confidences (not a distribution), you'll need calibration. Mapping raw scores to probabilities via sigmoid is another option for binary setups: sigmoid(score) = 1/(1+exp(-score)) but that treats each candidate separately and won't sum to 1.
Lauren (CS): I'll send this back to Acme. Quick Q: should we change the docs to make the semantics clearer? I can update but want the canonical wording.
Jia (ML): Yes please — docs should say: 'score' = raw model score (logit / log-odds style) returned by the reranker; not normalized; negative is allowed; use softmax to convert to distribution; use sigmoid for per-item confidence (not recommended for comparatives). Add examples and recommended stability trick (subtract max).
Paul (SRE): Also add a troubleshooting checklist for us and customers: include model name, request body, candidate ordering, whether any pre-filtering/tokenization was applied, and full response (we get better repro with exact bytes).
Devon (ENG): I'm going to add a small server-side convenience param in the feature tracker: `response_mode` with options `raw` (current), `softmax`, `sigmoid` — we'll flag it as experimental. For now, advise customers to post-process.
Acme Support (customer): Thanks! That clarifies a lot. We'll implement softmax client-side for now. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :raised_hands:
Lauren (CS): Great. Action items: I will reply to Acme with the snippet and doc language; Devon/Jia will open two tickets — one docs update, one feature flag for normalized output. Paul will add the checklist to triage playbook. I'll follow up when tickets land.
ops-bot: Created ticket CS-5234 for Acme follow-up (assigned to Lauren).
Lauren (CS): Thanks all. Following up in a few hours with the customer.
